doc.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29

title: Economy Hall balls and French Creole societies
summary: Jim remembers watching the band at Economy Hall balls and why it was named so; many benevolent organizations kept the bands busy.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I like one. You see, in my time, I know Jim as old as I am, when we go to the balls, you remember we were talking to the great economy hall. And they like that number stumbling. I'm going to bring you to around 21 and 22. Them numbers come out. We go to them big balls, like the church, you heard the Jim was giving the festival. Sam up there playing the music. I don't know if you're stuck about that. I'm up there watching Alfred on the drum and looking at the band play that number. You understand? And the rest of the day, you're stuck about no dancing. And you couldn't move me from that bandstand. Why did they call it economy hall, though? Oh, that's a French name, isn't it? French name, yeah. That's a French name, yeah. That was a cheap. It wasn't cheap, economy.
No, that's big organizations. Oh, society, benovine organizations. It's like the Jean's Army. Oh, let's go Creole. Part of French Creole. Then we had, oh, we had lots of benovine organizations.

We used to be playing with people having a good time dancing. Sure, man. We used to have so much dance here in this town until we didn't know who to go and play for. We had so many engagements. We were wondering who to play for.
